card.text: M10 is a globular star cluster in the Milky Way, about 5,070 parsecs away.

sources.label: Baumgardt & Vasiliev (2021), Accurate distances to Galactic globular clusters through a combination of Gaia EDR3, HST and literature data, MNRAS 505, 5957; Baumgardt's orbits table, NGC_6254: Rsun 5.07 ± 0.06 kpc
Wikipedia, "Messier 10"
sources.quote: Messier 10 or M10 is a globular cluster of stars in the equatorial constellation of Ophiuchus.

introduction.text: M10 is drawn as 2,840 of its member stars, measured by Gaia; each dot sits at its sky position, at the cluster's distance.

sources.label: Wikipedia, "Messier 10"
sources.quote: The object was discovered by the French astronomer Charles Messier on May 29, 1764, who cataloged it as number 10 in his catalogue and described it as a "nebula without stars".

members.title: Hunt & Reffert 2023 members
members.summary: One dot per member star inside the tidal radius, in its Gaia color. Its depth in the cluster is assumed, not measured.
